newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grain futures mostly lower in brisk Budapest trade.
newsitem.headline: Grain futures mostly lower in brisk Budapest trade.

text.p: Most grain contracts fell on the Budapest Commodity Exchange on continuing worries about export opportunities, although new wheat crop edged up slightly, dealers said.
"Prices continued to fall because there are still too few buyers on the market," said Mihaly Otvos of OTP Forex.
Maize closed at 18,500 forints a tonne for March, down 400, and at 18,000 for July, off 100. March wheat fell 400 to 27,810, while the October contract was up 70 at 22,170.
Turnover was 2,940 contracts, or 1.18 billion forints.
Otvos said Hungarian mills seemed to have built up excessive stocks of wheat, which they are unloading on the market.
Changes in the prices of the new wheat crop were speculative and insignificant, he added.
As for maize, the outlook remained negative with high domestic stocks and few potential economically accessible markets, he added.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
